script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.

- Western Russia: Russia attacks Ukraine with 170 drones overnight; 147 of them downed.

Full breakdown follows.

The Caribbean - bottom line: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
The United States-based software engineer accused of causing the leak of videos and photographs of a sexual encounter with a Jamaican attorney has lost a multimillion-dollar home in St Ann, which has been sold to settle a judgment handed down by the Supreme Court. Rodrick Brown, who resides in New York City, could possibly lose a second apartment as the attorney, Kimberley Facey, has filed documents in court seeking to recover millions of dollars in legal costs she incurred in pursuing the lawsuit against him.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russia attacks Ukraine with 170 drones overnight; 147 of them downed.
Russia attacked Ukraine with 170 strike drones overnight on 26-27 September. Ukrainian air defence downed 147 UAVs, while strikes were recorded at 18 locations.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Person killed in Russian attacks on Odesa, two others injured.
One person was killed and two others injured in a Russian attack on Odesa on the evening of 26 September. Emergency crews are dealing with the aftermath of the strike.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russian forces attack Kiliia in Odesa Oblast, damaging port and civilian infrastructure.
Russian forces attacked Kiliia in Odesa Oblast with strike drones overnight on 26-27 September, hitting port and civilian infrastructure. No casualties have been reported.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov claims Europe's military build-up could lead to war with Russia and says any conflict resulting from a European attack would be "short".

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said. Separately, two rescue workers were killed and another was injured when a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting bodies of victims from the blast. DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties from the blast.

British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and the army was examining a number of vehicles after security was stepped up at a British airbase used by US air forces in southwest England. The British government gave authorisation to the US to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. A Reuters eyewitness said armed police were blocking access to the main gate of the base.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: KP CM Afridi open to dialogue with govt but warns against 'misadventure'.
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday struck a conciliatory tone, offering to resolve issues with the federal government through dialogue but warned that any “misadventure” could result in serious repercussions. The PTI had been gearing up for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. However, CM Afridi announced a day ago that the march has been postponed to Oct 4.
